replies.author: Speccy_G
replies.body: It’s finished and we are now focused on marketing. Although coding was ai-assisted and the music you hear in the clip was also ai-generated, many assets were made by hand and I purchased a professional sound pack for the weapon sfx. I’ve been making 3d models for 18 years and the visuals are a deliberate choice. I am not saying that they cannot be improved further - visually some more contrast would be beneficial but the real issues lie with optimization. Some models have 70k polys… go on roast me for that one

comments.author: FailedGradAdmissions
comments.body:
Watched the video muted as I’m on my phone, didn’t know what people where complaining about. Then watched it with sound, yeah that music and effects are making you a disservice to put it lightly.

That aside you are further away than most. This could have passed for a niche Indie a decade ago and probably would have done well 2 decades ago. Those of you who played the alpha versions of Rimworld and and the old Dwarf Fortress know what I mean. Take that as a compliment OP.

Unfortunately, it’s 2026, and the bar is way higher right now. You’ll have to polish this, completely overhaul the music and then maybe you’ll have a successful Indie. Besides that price will matter a lot. This with fitting music, a good gameplay loop and for $9.99, yeah why not? People will buy it even with an AI disclaimer in Steam. But if you price it something like $40 yeah it won’t make it. So also be careful with the pricing once you put it for sale.

replies.author: Speccy_G
replies.body: Cheers, I agree on most accounts. OP is my wife lol, I made the game. I am banking exactly on an addictive gameplay loop and am pricing the game at 5,99 on Steam and for free on mobile (with ads). We have some decent multiplayer, our biggest issue is one lagging player currently ruins the experience for everyone in the match. But yeah, I’ll scrap that music, I got the message now lol
